title: Being inducted seven times and never serving
summary: Barnet went through draft induction seven times in New York without ever being taken, which led him to disband his band and move to California.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So you were inducted seven times, but were you actually in the service?
No, I never got in the service.
Why did they keep inducting you?

Well, I don't know. They kept calling me back and calling me back, but they had me in various -- I was in 1-A three times, and on every occasion I was -- something happened. They changed the -- they said, "No, you shouldn't be in 1-A." You should be here or there, and then the last time the war got over and the guy says well -- I really don't know. All I know --I knew everybody in New York. I made sure I went to New York, because I'd heard some terrible stories about what happened out on the coast here, over there. If you were a musician, you were in, you know, automatically. But in New York I knew everybody by their first name. "Oh, Charlie, are you here again?" I said, "Yeah, I'm here." You know. "Well, we don't have to tell you what to do. You know the routine."
Well, for how long a period of time did this go on?
Well, that's over a period of a couple of years.
It really messed up any plans you might make.

Well, you couldn't. That's why I disbanded the band and came out to California. Then when I'd get a call I'd grab a train and go back to New York, because I didn't change my -- I didn't want to change my -- well, I figured if I got inducted out in California I'd be sent to the Pacific, and I didn't dig that too much.
